analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. The reviewed changes are in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (a new sentence around head line 170 that I saw only in the file_changes patch excerpt, plus the head text at lines 952-1577) and docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md (a date bump and a reworded sentence at lines 3 and 92-93). No code, keys, authorization logic or wire handling changes.

The substantive documented change is that a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered coordinator session completes locally once accepted work and local response writes finish. This is performLifecycleDrain in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, which I could not see. Telemetry records state that coordinator_acknowledged is not claimed in that case. This broadens the earlier startup/scheduled-idle wording to cover reconnecting. It affects availability and lifecycle semantics (A-018, T-010, T-059), not confidentiality. A dead connection cannot deliver a drain acknowledgement, and the docs still say admission stays closed until a confirmed drain and reconnect where a barrier fenced the session. The code was not supplied, so whether draining without a session could skip response writes or reopen admission before the coordinator sees the state is an unverified contract and not a finding.

The remaining protocol-messages text in the supplied window (model replacement, prefix-cache receipts v2, prompt_work, GLM contract, autopilot, consent-gated fields) is context. I did not identify any weakened control relative to T-041, T-053 or T-056 in these lines. The prefix-cache receipt text keeps the nonce, sequence, scope and connection checks and states that a stale hint never grants a hit. Telemetry stays local and non-uploaded with no prompt or credential content.

For the next pass: confirm that performLifecycleDrain matches the documented behavior, namely no admission reopening and no acknowledged-drain claim without a session.
